comment: Highest-priority issue for us at HISP: the categorical statement that HMIS ‘is not foundational’ is analytically unsound across country contexts. A national RHIS platform can be both a business service and infrastructure when multiple programmes depend on its shared organisational hierarchy, metadata, aggregate repository, analytics, APIs, user management and support network. For many LMICs, the DHIS2-based HMIS is the most established national digital health infrastructure; classifying it only as downstream risks misdirecting investment toward new registries/LHR services while weakening what is already distributed, operational, and cost-effiicient.

public.text: Highest-priority issue for us at HISP: the categorical statement that HMIS ‘is not foundational’ is analytically unsound across country contexts. A national RHIS platform can be both a business service and infrastructure when multiple programmes depend on its shared organisational hierarchy, metadata, aggregate repository, analytics, APIs, user management and support network. For many LMICs, the DHIS2-based HMIS is the most established national digital health infrastructure; classifying it only as downstream risks misdirecting investment toward new registries/LHR services while weakening what is already distributed, operational, and cost-effiicient.
public.suggestedRevision: Remove the categorical ‘not foundational’ statement. Use a functional/contextual test: an HMIS/RHIS platform may be foundational, shared-platform or business-service infrastructure depending on national reuse, dependency, governance and scale. In Figure 2.1 and Appendix C, show HMIS/RHIS spanning foundational and business-service layers where it supplies shared platform capabilities.
